newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU clears aid to German shipyard Meyer.
newsitem.headline: EU clears aid to German shipyard Meyer.

text.p: The European Commission has rejected a Finnish complaint and cleared subsidies paid to German shipyard Jos L. Meyer GmbH to help it win a contract to build two luxury cruise ships for Malaysian company Genting International, an EU source said on Monday.
Finnish-based rival Kvaerner Masa-Yards, which bid unsuccessfully for the same contract, had complained that the subsidies had been instrumental in securing the deal for Meyer.
French shipyard Saint Nazaire also put in a bid.
In December last year, the Finnish government asked the European Union executive to investigate the case under EU rules on shipbuilding aid.
The Commission established in a decision in July that the aid "did not distort intra-Community competition and therefore the Commission allowed the aid," the source said.
The aid amounted to 6.5 percent of the contract value.
Meyer offered to build the two ships called Superstar Leo and Superstar Virgo for about 2.5 million European currency units each, a Commission official said earlier this year.
EU rules allow for aid of up to nine percent of the contract value, but when two or more EU shipyards compete for the same order, the aid granted is not allowed to distort competition.
